description: Versioned 6-item deductive coding rubric for EMNLP 2020-2026 papers. Separates policy applicability, practice applicability, 4-state evidence status (distinguishing not_applicable, not_reported, explicitly_reported_inadequate, and adequately_reported), and derived compliance.

evidence_status_definitions.not_applicable: The reporting item does not apply to the paper's methodology (e.g., purely theoretical/survey paper with no compute experiments for C1, or no external datasets/models/code reused for B2).
evidence_status_definitions.not_reported: The reporting item applies to the paper, but no section, statement, or mention of the target information appears anywhere in the main text or ordinary appendices.
evidence_status_definitions.explicitly_reported_inadequate: The paper explicitly mentions the topic or includes a relevant heading, but the content fails substantive rubric requirements (e.g., generic boilerplate 'Our work has limitations', future-work wishes only, hardware name without training duration/GPU-hours, or claiming 'no ethical issues' on sensitive personal/demographic data).
evidence_status_definitions.adequately_reported: The paper provides concrete, qualifying evidence in the main text or ordinary appendices satisfying all substantive requirements of the item.

derived_compliance_rules.Compliant: policy_applies == true AND practice_applies == true AND evidence_status == 'adequately_reported'
derived_compliance_rules.Non-compliant: policy_applies == true AND practice_applies == true AND evidence_status IN ['not_reported', 'explicitly_reported_inadequate']
derived_compliance_rules.Not applicable: policy_applies == false OR practice_applies == false (Note: practice presence is still tracked via evidence_status for longitudinal adoption series!)
derived_compliance_rules.Uncertain: practice_applies == 'uncertain' OR extraction/parsing failure prevents verification

items.name: Limitations section (Structural)
items.practice_applicability_rule: Applies to ALL research papers (always true).

criteria.adequately_reported: Contains a dedicated standalone section or clearly marked subsection/paragraph titled 'Limitations' (or 'Limitations and Future Work' / 'Ethics and Limitations') located in the main paper or before References.
criteria.explicitly_reported_inadequate: Discusses limitations only embedded inside Conclusion/Discussion without any explicit 'Limitations' heading, OR places the 'Limitations' section only inside an external appendix when required in the main paper.
criteria.not_reported: No 'Limitations' heading and no identifiable limitations section.

negative_examples: A final paragraph inside '5. Conclusion' starting with 'One limitation of our study is...' without a heading (coded as explicitly_reported_inadequate for structural section presence).

items.name: Specific limitation (Substantive)
items.practice_applicability_rule: Applies to ALL research papers (always true).

criteria.adequately_reported: States at least one concrete methodological assumption, scope restriction (e.g., language/domain/compute boundary), or empirical failure mode AND its consequence for validity, performance, or generalisation.
criteria.explicitly_reported_inadequate: Contains only generic boilerplate disclaimers ('Our method has some limitations'), purely future-work statements ('In the future we plan to test more languages'), or disguised strengths ('Our model requires only a single GPU').
criteria.not_reported: No discussion of limitations anywhere in the paper or ordinary appendices.

positive_examples: The model assumes accurate transcripts; automatic speech recognition errors in noisy environments may substantially reduce downstream classification accuracy.
negative_examples: Our method has limitations that we will address in future work.
We will test other languages in future work.

items.name: Ethical risks and broader impact
items.checklist_code: ARR Responsible NLP Section A / EMNLP 2022+ Ethics
items.practice_applicability_rule: Conditional: true if the paper collects human/crowdsourced data, processes personal/demographic/clinical/social-media text, or develops models with plausible dual-use, bias, misinformation, or safety risks; false for purely formal/mathematical/syntactic studies without sensitive data or societal risk.

criteria.adequately_reported: Identifies at least one concrete ethical issue, societal risk, dual-use concern, bias, or human-subject protection measure (e.g., anonymisation, IRB, annotator pay) relevant to the work and discusses its implications or mitigation.
criteria.explicitly_reported_inadequate: Includes an 'Ethics Statement' or 'Broader Impact' heading that contains only a boilerplate denial ('This work has no ethical issues' or 'We use public data so there are no ethical concerns') despite handling sensitive/human/LLM generation tasks.
criteria.not_reported: No Ethics Statement section and no discussion of ethical concerns anywhere in the paper despite relevant ethical/data risks.
criteria.not_applicable: Paper has no human subjects, sensitive data, or plausible dual-use/societal harm risks, and either omits ethics or states non-applicability.

positive_examples: Because our dataset is scraped from Reddit discussions on mental health, we remove all usernames and paraphrase quotes to prevent re-identification, though residual demographic bias Toward English-speaking users remains.
negative_examples: Ethics Statement: Our work uses publicly available benchmark datasets and therefore raises no ethical concerns.

items.name: Computational budget (Checklist C1)
items.practice_applicability_rule: Conditional: true if the paper runs computational experiments (training, fine-tuning, or large-scale model inference/evaluation); false for purely theoretical or non-computational survey papers.

criteria.adequately_reported: Reports total or per-run computational budget with explicit time/energy units (e.g., GPU-hours, CPU-hours, training wall-clock time + hardware count such as '4 hours on 2x NVIDIA A100 GPUs', FLOPs, or kWh/CO2 estimates).
criteria.explicitly_reported_inadequate: Mentions hardware type only (e.g., 'We trained our models on NVIDIA V100 GPUs') or software framework without any training duration, GPU-hours, or compute budget.
criteria.not_reported: Runs computational experiments but mentions neither compute hardware nor training time/budget.

positive_examples: Fine-tuning LLaMA-7B took approximately 6.5 hours on 4 NVIDIA A100 (80GB) GPUs (26 GPU-hours per run).
negative_examples: All experiments were conducted using PyTorch on NVIDIA A100 GPUs.

items.name: Asset licensing (Checklist B2)
items.checklist_code: ARR Checklist B2 (Use of Existing Scientific Artifacts)
items.practice_applicability_rule: Conditional: true if the paper uses, adapts, or releases any dataset, pretrained model, or code repository; false only if no external or new artifacts are used.

criteria.adequately_reported: Explicitly names the licence or terms of use (e.g., 'CC BY 4.0', 'MIT License', 'Apache-2.0', 'LDC User Agreement') for reused or released datasets, models, or code, OR explicitly states that the upstream licence is unspecified/unknown after checking.
criteria.explicitly_reported_inadequate: Cites datasets/models or provides a GitHub/HuggingFace URL, or says 'publicly available datasets', without naming any licence or terms of use in the paper or appendices.
criteria.not_reported: Uses datasets/models/code without any mention of availability, terms, or licensing.
criteria.not_applicable: Paper uses no datasets, pretrained models, or code artifacts.

positive_examples: We evaluate on SQuAD 2.0 (distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0) and release our code under the MIT License.
negative_examples: All datasets used in this study are publicly available for research purposes.

items.name: AI writing/coding assistance disclosure
items.checklist_code: ACL 2023 Policy on AI Writing Assistance
items.practice_applicability_rule: Descriptive indicator across all papers (true use is unobserved when undisclosed; missing disclosure is NOT coded as non-compliance).

criteria.adequately_reported: Explicitly discloses the AI tool used (e.g., ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Grammarly, Claude) AND the scope of assistance (e.g., grammar editing, code autocompletion) in the text or Acknowledgments.
criteria.explicitly_reported_inadequate: Mentions using 'an AI tool' or 'LLM assistance' for writing/coding without specifying either the tool or the scope/accountability.
criteria.not_reported: No mention of AI writing or coding assistance (note: represents absence of disclosure, not non-compliance).
criteria.not_applicable: Used only if explicitly pre-2023 and evaluating post-2023 policy window, though tracked descriptively across all years.

positive_examples: We used ChatGPT (GPT-4) solely for grammar correction and polishing of author-written drafts.
negative_examples: AI tools were used during the preparation of this manuscript.
